The original planning baseline did not execute application changes or provider calls. Later authorized execution passes record their narrow source fixes, automated/browser evidence and remaining provider/product gates in their domain reports. Explicit characterization of a limitation is not approval of it for launch.

Use the system map first, then fixtures/runbook, domain scenarios and the release gate. Tables and parameterized scenarios are executable checklists: record each named variant separately, and fail the parent scenario if any required variant fails. Counts below count unique test IDs, not each permutation or browser viewport. An API role case and a unit case intentionally cover different layers of the same capability.

## System map

| Role | Current authority |
|---|---|
| anonymous | Active catalogue/detail/effective availability, public media, auth/recovery, Mollie webhook and health. Policy content currently requires login. |
| SCOUT | Own requests/bookings/inquiries; checkout and cancellation; own paid receipts; participant incidents; policy acceptance. |
| OWNER | Own venues/availability/production/media; verification and payout destination submission; request/inquiry decisions; confirmed cancellation; own payouts/statements and participant incidents. |
| ADMIN | Operational queues/reviews, booking read/accept/decline/cancel/full refund, payouts/liabilities, policy lifecycle, incident resolution; privileged receipts/statements. Not a universal substitute for OWNER-only endpoints. |

Shared dependencies: PostgreSQL 16 native enums/arrays, row locks and exclusion/unique constraints; Flyway common V1–V14 and local-only V100–V103; JWT/database user authority; Clock in selected time policies (other services use OffsetDateTime.now); transactional notification intents and bounded asynchronous outbox dispatch; Mollie payment/refund/reporting client; Gemini parser/ranker; Resend; local/S3 public media and private document stores; AES-GCM/HMAC bank protection. Optional Next Cala BFF is separately tested and has no Spring trust authority.

### Scheduled work

All six scheduled methods are covered by JOB cases: request/payment expiry (same job), inquiry offer expiry, payout readiness, auth recovery-token cleanup, Mollie fee reconciliation and workflow observability. There is no separate general refund-polling scheduler or durable email outbox. Provider callback/replay paths must reconcile refunds.

Metrics inventory (JOB-006, OPS-007, SEC-003/006 and AUTO observability): counters `eema.workflow.booking.approval.expired`, `eema.workflow.booking.request.expired`, `eema.workflow.booking.request.unavailable`, `eema.workflow.payment.late.detected`, `eema.workflow.refund.automatic.initiated`, `eema.workflow.inquiry.offer.expired`; gauges `eema.workflow.payment.creation.stuck`, `eema.workflow.refund.stuck`, `eema.workflow.mollie.fee.unreconciled`, `eema.workflow.payout.held`, `eema.workflow.payout.ready`, `eema.workflow.payout.overdue`, `eema.workflow.owner.liability.open`; recovery counters `eema.auth.email.verification.completed`, `eema.auth.password.reset.completed`. For each metric capture baseline, commit one eligible event or seed one qualifying row, scan/query, require expected delta/value, replay and ensure no duplicate increment. Inspect meter tags: no user/booking/payment IDs. Read metric through ADMIN-only actuator endpoint. Counter reset on process restart is not a persistent financial ledger.

<a id="execution-contract"></a>
## Levels, priorities and environment matrix

| Level | Evidence required |
|---|---|
| UNIT | Explicit domain decision/validation/formatting assertions with controlled clock/mocks. |
| INTEGRATION | Collaborating services/controllers/storage or real database; say whether repositories are mocked. |
| API | Actual HTTP status/body/headers and actor/ownership checks; mock MVC evidence is narrower than live HTTP. |
| LOCAL E2E | Browser→Next→Spring→local PostgreSQL flow; external boundaries stubbed only through an available test harness. |
| STAGING E2E | Deployed origins, real sandbox providers, persistent staging database/storage and actual email delivery. |
| SECURITY | Negative access, object identity, input, secret, storage and transport probes. |
| CONCURRENCY | Independent transactions/workers released from a barrier; inspect committed final state. |
| MANUAL UX | Browser/keyboard/screen-reader/responsive/copy review with screenshots. |
| OPERATIONAL | Startup/jobs/metrics/logging/configuration/backup/recovery evidence. |

P0 = auth/security, money, state integrity or release-blocking operations. P1 = core marketplace/trust/admin workflow. P2 = important interaction, presentation and nonfinancial edge behavior. P3 = secondary/polish or trivial existing harness checks. A failing security or financial invariant discovered in a P2 visual check is escalated to P0; priority never weakens a required assertion.

| Environment | What can be proved | Limits / use |
|---|---|---|
| LOCAL MOCKED | Existing Java service/controller tests, parser/ranker fixtures, provider payloads, PDF rendering, crypto, fixed-clock boundaries | No database locking, actual browser/provider/delivery or bucket IAM proof. |
| LOCAL REAL POSTGRES | Testcontainers constraints/locking; local Docker browser/API/persistence; isolated backup/restore | Existing Testcontainer mocks are test-class scoped, not a browser-accessible fake-provider application profile. Browser payment/AI portions require a separately prepared isolated stub harness or must be BLOCKED locally. Direct quote can bypass Gemini for local request QA. |
| LOCAL MOLLIE TEST | Optional real TEST checkout and manual callback per backend README | Requires test key and explicitly enabled external testing; local callback POST causes real provider GET. Cannot prove public callback delivery without public routing. Never use live key. Not executed for this documentation task. |
| STAGING | Real Mollie TEST callbacks/refunds, Resend delivery, Gemini behavior, S3 IAM/durability, TLS/CORS/proxy/restarts | Mandatory for provider/hosting proof; fee reporting may remain BLOCKED if sandbox cannot expose authoritative cost. |
| PRIVATE ALPHA | Gate-approved staging-like release with controlled participants and operating support | Run P0/P1 regression and actual provider/support drills; use approved business inputs, not test legal content. |
| PRODUCTION SMOKE | Health, TLS/security headers, active catalogue, existing authorized history and navigation | Read-only and separately authorized. No fixture reset, synthetic legal publication, charge/refund, bank reveal or mark-paid smoke. |

Each scenario has one primary environment for count clarity. LOCAL REAL POSTGRES scenarios should also be rehearsed in staging when they exercise browser/API behavior; LOCAL MOCKED cases remain fast CI tests. PROVIDER cases are the mandatory staging-only layer. PostgreSQL and staging requirements are not interchangeable.

### Result contract for every scenario

Record `test ID / variant / commit pair / environment / tester / UTC time / PASS|FAIL|BLOCKED|NOT RUN / evidence / defect ID / cleanup`. PASS requires every stated expected UI/API/domain/provider/security observation, including no forbidden side effects. FAIL means an observed mismatch; BLOCKED means missing fixture, clock control, approved policy, provider or infrastructure. Never convert a documented limitation to a PASS on its acceptance criterion merely because source predicts it. UNIT scenarios explicitly say UI N/A; manual browser behavior is covered separately.

### Financial and time oracles

`durationMinutes = Duration.between(startTime,endTime).toMinutes()`; `billableMinutes=max(durationMinutes, minimumBookingMinutes)`; `hourlyTotal=HALF_UP(hourlyRate × billableMinutes / 60, 2)`; `venuePriceEur=min(hourlyTotal, normalized fullDayRate)` when cap exists. There is no independent “must physically book minimum duration” rejection. Price snapshots remain immutable across owner edits/acceptance/checkout.

Cancellation grace is inclusive through confirmation+24h **only when shoot is strictly more than 48h away**. Outside grace: >7d full; exactly 7d through exactly 48h partial 50%; <48h zero. Owner/admin confirmed cancellation always full with required reason and different provider-cost responsibility. Use cancellation snapshots and instants across DST. Refund cents HALF_UP; retained=paid−refund; commission on retained uses stored percentage; owner entitlement cannot be negative.

Local profile commission is 4.00%, base configuration default is 20.00% (overridable). Capture effective profile/config for each run, do not silently standardize prices or rates. Booking response/payment deadlines are now+configured hours (24h default), **not capped to shoot start**; inquiry offer expiry is capped to slot start. Checkout exempts a valid accepted booking from fresh lead-time checks.

## Fixture cookbook and local runbook


Use a unique `RUN` suffix for each run and keep a local fixture manifest mapping aliases to returned UUIDs. Do not use production people, email/phone/bank data. `.test` addresses are non-deliverable: local tests capture messages; staging delivery needs an approved nonpersonal QA mailbox on a controlled test domain.

| Alias | Fictional account | State variants |
|---|---|---|
| Scout A | `scout-a+RUN@example.test`, QA Scout A | Owns booking/inquiry; create separate unverified/inactive copy. |
| Scout B | `scout-b+RUN@example.test`, QA Scout B | Unrelated ownership/competing scout. |
| Owner A | `owner-a+RUN@example.test`, QA Owner A | Owns standard venues; UNVERIFIED/PENDING/VERIFIED/REJECTED copies. |
| Owner B | `owner-b+RUN@example.test`, QA Owner B | Owns separate venue/bank/payout, never authorized for A. |
| Admin | `admin+RUN@example.test`, QA Admin | Provision via isolated local SQL fixture or existing staging admin process; public ADMIN registration prohibited. |

Fixture password `QaFixture-2026!` is test-only. Phone can be omitted; use literal synthetic string `QA-PHONE-001` for unconstrained phone text tests, not a real number. Use structurally valid published test IBAN `NL91ABNA0417164300` only as a local/mock validation fixture and **never execute a transfer to it**; replacement test IBANs come from IbanPolicyTest. Do not assume a structurally valid test number belongs to a bank sandbox.

Set `T0` to a recorded UTC instant, seconds/nanos zero for minute tests. `D0` is its Europe/Amsterdam local date; `D14=D0+14 days`, `D15=D0+15 days`. Give all days identical weekly hours to avoid dependence on weekday. For DST derive the next zone transition with ZoneRules in existing Java test harness rather than hardcoding a date. API/browser tests cannot freeze all current services with the injected Clock: use far-future slots and controlled fixture timestamps for expiry, and existing unit tests for exact boundaries. Never change a shared host clock.

These are test data choices, not new business rules.

### Start and inspect locally

Do not overwrite existing `.env` files or print secrets. Backend local startup uses repository README/Docker Compose. Java tests require JDK21/Maven on host; Docker builds can run normal application without host Java. These commands are instructions for a future authorized test run, not evidence they were executed here.

```bash
cd ~/workspace/Eema-backend
docker compose up --build -d
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/api/actuator/health
mvn test
mvn verify -Ppostgres-integration
# In another terminal:
cd ~/workspace/Eema-frontend
npm run dev
# TypeScript/lint/build checks (no browser-test framework currently installed):
npm run check
```

For LOCAL MOCKED do not configure external keys. Existing tests replace providers inside the test class; there is no documented mock-provider server profile for an entire browser session. For LOCAL REAL POSTGRES browser flows avoid matching via direct venue quote when Gemini unavailable, and stop payment portions at provider boundary unless a controlled test harness has been prepared. A simulated browser response alone proves UI only and must not be recorded as backend E2E.

### Concrete API fixture sequence

Use a REST client with environment variables `API`, `SCOUT_TOKEN`, `OWNER_TOKEN`, `ADMIN_TOKEN`, `VENUE`, `BOOKING`; store tokens privately, never paste into the report. Set `API=http://localhost:8080/api`. HTTP examples use variable placeholders resolved by that client.

1. `POST {{API}}/auth/register` with `{"email":"scout-a+RUN@example.test","password":"QaFixture-2026!","fullName":"QA Scout A","role":"SCOUT"}`; save `user.id`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken`. Repeat owner and second personas with separate role/email.
2. Local notification fixture captures verification token; `POST /auth/verify-email {"token":"captured value"}`. SQL `email_verified=true` is allowed only for isolated non-email test setup, and is not proof verification worked. Local ADMIN setup: register a fixture account, then parameterized SQL update its `users.role` to `ADMIN` and email_verified true; login afresh. Follow existing staging admin runbook instead on shared environments.
3. Create five **local test-only** policies as ADMIN using `POST /admin/policies {"policyType":"TERMS_OF_SERVICE","version":"QA-RUN-v1","title":"QA fixture only","effectiveAt":"<T0 ISO offset>","content":"TEST FIXTURE — NOT LEGAL CONTENT"}`, repeating every PolicyType; publish each returned ID. Never publish these placeholders to real participant environments.
4. As scout/owner `GET /policies/current`; accept actual returned IDs using `POST /policies/accept {"policyVersionIds":["<ID1>","<ID2>","<ID3>","<ID4>","<ID5>"]}`.
5. As owner `POST /owner/verification/submit {"note":"QA review"}`; admin `POST /admin/owner-verifications/{id}/approve {"verificationMethod":"MANUAL_REVIEW","note":"QA fixture"}`.
6. Create Studio with payload below, capture `id` as VENUE. Upload multipart `file` to `/venues/{{VENUE}}/photos`; copy returned photoPaths. Save timezone/settings and weekly schedule. Submit `/venues/{{VENUE}}/submit-for-review`; admin approve `/admin/venues/{{VENUE}}/approve` with optional note.
7. Scout request payload below to `/bookings`, capture BOOKING. Owner `POST /bookings/{{BOOKING}}/accept` (no body); scout `POST /bookings/{{BOOKING}}/checkout` (no amount body) only under prepared mocked/test-provider environment.
8. Callback is `POST /webhooks/mollie/payment`, `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, body `id=<authoritative mock/test payment ID>`. It fetches Mollie state; this is not a fake “paid=true” switch.

```json
{
  "name":"QA Studio RUN", "neighbourhood":"QA District", "sizeM2":120,
  "hourlyRateEur":100.00, "minimumBookingMinutes":60, "minimumLeadTimeMinutes":120,
  "fullDayRateEur":null, "maxCrewSize":12,
  "permittedActivities":["PHOTO","VIDEO"], "prohibitedActivities":[],
  "naturalLight":true, "blackoutPossible":true, "ceilingHeightM":3.5,
  "loadingAccess":true, "parkingAvailable":true, "parkingSpaces":2, "floorNumber":0,
  "liftAvailable":false, "wheelchairAccessible":true, "bathroomsAvailable":true,

  "powerDetails":"QA fixture power specification", "tags":["qa"],

}
```

`PUT /venues/{id}` requires the same complete body plus `"timezone":"Europe/Amsterdam","photoPaths":["<actual uploaded reference>"]`. Creation has no timezone or photoPaths fields. Weekly request: `{"intervals":[{"dayOfWeek":"MONDAY","startTime":"09:00","endTime":"17:00"}]}`; add remaining six days explicitly for the standard fixture. Override: `{"date":"<D14>","startTime":"11:00","endTime":"12:00","type":"BLOCKED","allDay":false}`; all-day uses null times. Booking request:

```json
{
  "venueId":"<VENUE UUID>", "shootDate":"<D14 YYYY-MM-DD>",
  "startTime":"09:15", "endTime":"13:45", "rawBrief":"QA photo shoot with 4 people",
  "scoutContact":{"name":"QA Scout A","email":"scout-a+RUN@example.test","phone":null}
}
```

Inquiry create: `venueId, requestedDate, requestedStartTime, requestedEndTime, message`; offer: `offeredDate, offeredStartTime, offeredEndTime`. Cancel: optional scout `reason`, required owner/admin `reason`; incident: `category, description`; resolve: `resolutionNote`; destination: `accountHolderName, iban`; mark paid: `externalTransferReference`. Exact required/null/length constraints for **every** request DTO are embedded in INPUT cases. GET filters and method signatures are in API cases and endpoint matrix.

### Observe and reset state

Use read-only SQL for evidence on: users, refresh_tokens, email_verification_tokens, password_reset_tokens; venues/venue_operating_hours/venue_availability_overrides; bookings/booking_events/availability_inquiries; owner_payouts/owner_financial_liabilities/owner_payout_destinations; financial_documents; policy_versions/policy_acceptances/booking_policy_versions; owner_verifications/marketplace_trust_events/incident_reports. Confirm exact column names against common migrations before scripting; inspect hashes/counts, never export raw bank ciphertext keys or auth credentials. Record source/target status, immutable snapshots, row/event count, updated timestamps and provider IDs privately.

Prefer a per-run disposable database and restore the baseline between destructive variants. Targeted deletion requires an explicit transaction and child-first dependency order from migrations; RESTRICT relationships should fail rather than be disabled. Existing Postgres test class truncates its own disposable users/policy fixtures with CASCADE, not shared data. A normal restart is `docker compose restart backend`. **`docker compose down -v` permanently deletes all local database, uploaded-media and private-document volumes.** Only use it on disposable local stack after backup and then `docker compose up --build -d` to reseed. Compose hardcodes container names/ports: a project name alone does not isolate a parallel stack; use a prepared override or separate DB/host ports.

### Backup/restore drill commands (disposable local only)

```bash
cd ~/workspace/Eema-backend
docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dump -U eema -d eema -Fc > /tmp/eema-qa-backup.dump
docker compose exec -T postgres createdb -U eema eema_qa_restore
docker compose exec -T postgres pg_restore -U eema -d eema_qa_restore --no-owner < /tmp/eema-qa-backup.dump
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U eema -d eema_qa_restore -c 'SELECT version, success FROM flyway_schema_history ORDER BY installed_rank'
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U eema -d eema_qa_restore -c 'SELECT status, count(*) FROM bookings GROUP BY status'
```

Start the same backend artifact with datasource pointing to `eema_qa_restore`, a separate port and copied fixture storage; disable emails/reporting/provider credentials. Validate health, representative authorized reads, bank decrypt using retained fixture keys and PDF hashes. Preserve source counts before dump. Restore object volumes separately; record recovery duration and data loss point, with acceptable RTO/RPO supplied by operations (not invented here). Cleanup: stop restore instance, explicitly verify database name, drop only `eema_qa_restore` after retaining evidence; remove private local dump when no longer required. Managed staging snapshot/PITR and object-store recovery still require staging rehearsal.

<a id="family-auth"></a>
### AUTH scenarios

Auth-input contract update (2026-09-10): register/login/resend/forgot email is trimmed and lowercased before validation; registration fullName trims outer whitespace only. Passwords and tokens remain exact. All six auth body DTOs reject unknown properties with safe 400 responses; only SCOUT and OWNER are self-service roles. These rules supersede older generic auth template assumptions. Database V1 already enforces unique LOWER(email); no migration added.

<a id="auth-001"></a>
#### AUTH-001 — Register SCOUT

**Test ID:** AUTH-001. **Area:** AUTH. **Priority:** P0 (public account creation, role escalation and credential integrity). **Test level:** API, INTEGRATION, LOCAL E2E, SECURITY. **Result:** AUTH-001A **PASS** (2026-09-10, hardened contract, local API/integration/browser); AUTH-001B **NOT RUN** (staging delivery). See dated [execution record](qa/AUTH-001_REGISTER_SCOUT.md#corrected-contract-execution-record). Re-executed in the complete AUTH pass; [current evidence](qa/AUTH_EXECUTION_REPORT.md). Historical Unicode password failures in AUTH-004/AUTH-014 were resolved by the approved Argon2id launch fix; see the current AUTH report.

**Roles involved:** Anonymous visitor → newly registered SCOUT. A valid existing SCOUT token is an optional-header security subcase, not a denial case. OWNER registration remains AUTH-002. Registration does not accept an owner/scout resource UUID for authorization.

**Preconditions:** Backend and PostgreSQL healthy; frontend healthy for browser checks; `/api/auth/register` reachable; generated email absent. No existing user, verified email, policy acceptance, owner verification, venue or booking is required. Use local email-disabled configuration, or an explicitly authorized staging delivery mailbox for variant B. Never send provider delivery to `example.test`.

**Test data:** `RUN_ID=$(scripts/qa-run-id.sh)`, `scout-a+$RUN_ID@example.test`, full name `QA Scout A`, synthetic password `QaFixture-2026!`, role `SCOUT`. Generate a separate RUN_ID for API and browser registrations. No hard-coded user UUID or seed deletion. API normalization test submits two surrounding spaces plus the uppercase address and `  QA Scout A  `; expect canonical lowercase email and `QA Scout A`. Password bytes/characters are unchanged.

**Exact steps:**

1. Follow the companion guide's startup/health checks; generate the fresh fixture. Open `/` in a separate browser profile, choose **Sign in / register**, then the **Create account** tab.
2. Fill full name, choose **Scout**, enter email/password, and submit once. Observe one `POST /api/auth/register`; inspect status and field names without exporting token-bearing response bodies or HARs.
3. Confirm the registration panel closes to the marketplace at `/` when entered through the header with no pending matching brief. Check identity, Scout navigation and **Email not verified**.
4. Reload before access expiry. Confirm cached authenticated SCOUT state and `emailVerified=false` persist. Separately issue authenticated `GET /api/auth/me` and compare its user DTO. Do not claim reload itself invokes `/auth/me`.
5. Inspect safe database aggregates from the guide; run `mvn verify -Ppostgres-integration` for actual Argon2id matching, both token hash correspondences, expiry and transaction assertions. Do not try to recover verification secrets from the database.
6. Run the security/rejection subcases below with new fixtures where applicable. Sign out and remove temporary response evidence after recording sanitized results.

**Expected UI behavior:** `AuthProvider.completeSession` persists access/refresh tokens, expiresIn, user and storedAt under localStorage `eema:auth`; subscribers update immediately. Header shows `QA Scout A · Scout`, **My bookings**, **Inquiries**, **Email not verified**, **Sign out**. Registration through the header returns to idle marketplace; no route redirect. A pending matching brief is a separate flow. Browsing remains available. The API client blocks authenticated non-GET, non-admin mutations for an unverified account; backend verified-email/policy gates remain authoritative on their applicable endpoints. A **Policy review required** link depends on a successful policy-status response; registration neither requires nor creates acceptances. Reload reads cached session; compare `/auth/me` explicitly, without implying cache restoration validates the JWT.

**Expected API/backend behavior:** Anonymous `POST /api/auth/register` returns **201 Created**, JSON with exactly `accessToken` (nonempty signed JWT), `refreshToken` (nonempty opaque token), `tokenType` (`Bearer`), `expiresIn` (seconds; current 900), `user`. User fields are exactly `id` (UUID), `email` (lowercase, plus suffix preserved), `role=SCOUT`, `fullName=QA Scout A`, `phone=null`, `active=true`, `emailVerified=false`. No password/hash/verification token appears. JWT is issued for the new user, not an optional authenticated caller. `/api/auth/me` returns 200 and the same user. Record constructors invoke `EmailNormalizer` before Jakarta validation. Padded mixed-case email succeeds and persists trimmed/lowercase; internal whitespace and invalid format still fail `@Email`. Registration fullName is trimmed at its edges, preserving internal spaces. No Gmail-specific normalization.

**Expected database/domain state:** One new `users` row with returned UUID, normalized email, exact full_name, SCOUT, active=true, email_verified=false; password_hash is self-describing Argon2id (default memory 65536 KiB, iterations 3, parallelism 1), differs from raw password and satisfies `PasswordEncoder.matches(raw, hash)`. One `refresh_tokens` row for that user, revoked=false, expiry approximately registration time + configured 7 days, token_hash equal to lowercase SHA-256 hex of returned raw refresh token and unequal to the raw token. One `email_verification_tokens` row, used_at NULL, expiry approximately injected Clock time + configured 24 hours, token_hash equal to `OneTimeTokenCodec.hash` of the transient event token. Both token hashes have 64 hex characters; neither raw token is stored. No policy acceptance is implied. HTTP status, response fields and header copy are not database columns. Verification persistence failure rolls the user/token transaction back; post-commit delivery failure preserves committed state.

**Expected email/provider behavior:** Success publishes exactly one `EmailVerificationRequestedEvent(userId, rawToken)`. `AccountEmailEventListener` captures a credential-placeholder artifact synchronously BEFORE_COMMIT in the same transaction; the durable worker sends after commit. Notification recipient is the normalized email; subject **Verify your Eema email**; CTA `/verify-email?token=<transient-token>` at configured frontend base URL, with configured expiry and verification-required wording. Raw verification token is transient notification content, never the auth response or a DB column. Provider failure cannot undo registration. OPS-DEC-001 adds durable retry; the outbox stores only a nonsecret derivation nonce/hash reference and credential-placeholder content, never the raw token or a credential-bearing URL. See OPS-008 for dispatch/recovery semantics.

- **AUTH-001A — LOCAL EMAIL DISABLED:** `EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED=false`; token/event still created; notification adapter may execute, but `EmailService` skips Resend. Registration succeeds. This variant requires no real email delivery.
- **AUTH-001B — STAGING EMAIL ENABLED:** authorized controlled mailbox, configured sender/base URL and enabled Resend; verify one attempt, actual receipt, correct subject/CTA and expiry copy. Delivery is NOT RUN until proven in staging; synthetic local `.test` addresses cannot prove it. Do not click verification before completing the unverified-state checks.
- Rejected request: no new user/token records and no verification event/email attempt for that request. Duplicate registration leaves the first account's existing records unchanged.

**Security expectation / focused subcases:** These are assertion variants of AUTH-001, not extra master scenario IDs.

| Subcase | Exact action | Expected result / side effects |
|---|---|---|
| Public endpoint | Submit valid SCOUT payload anonymously | 201, new SCOUT |
| Optional authenticated actor | Repeat with fresh email and valid existing SCOUT Bearer token | 201, new distinct user; caller identity does not override payload |
| ADMIN / unsupported role | Replace role with `ADMIN`, then `SUPERUSER`, using new addresses | 400; no user, tokens or event |
| Unknown-field / mass assignment | Add each of `active`, `emailVerified`, `id`, `passwordHash`, `ownerVerificationStatus`, `createdAt`, or an arbitrary field separately to a valid payload | 400 with safe existing JSON error; no user/token/event/email. Login, refresh, verify-email, resend-verification, forgot-password and reset-password are strict too; unrelated API JSON behavior is unchanged. |
| Duplicate / case collision | Register once, resubmit padded uppercase equivalent email | 409; exactly one original user and one token of each kind; no extra event/email |
| Invalid inputs | Invalid email or internal email whitespace, 5-character password, 73-character password, 1-character fullName, missing role, malformed `{` body | 400; no registration side effects. Password policy is 8–72 characters, not an invented complexity rule |
| Persistence fault | Integration test injects verification-token save failure | Safe 500; transaction rolls back user and both token types; no event/email |
| Post-commit notification fault | Integration test injects delivery adapter exception | 201 persists; one attempt, no rollback; delivery itself failed |

**Cleanup/reset:** Sign out, close isolated browser profile, discard raw responses/tokens; fixture rows can remain with RUN_ID. Preserve seed users/venues. Between full local suites only, run `scripts/reset-local-qa.sh --dry-run`, then explicitly `--confirm-destroy-local-qa` to delete all guarded local Compose database/media/document volumes and reseed. There is no snapshot-restore harness or targeted FK deletion step. Never apply this reset to staging. Testcontainers owns/discards its separate disposable database.

**Automation recommendation:** ALREADY AUTOMATED after this change: `RegistrationIntegrationTest` (11 methods) covers real HTTP/security, PostgreSQL/hash/expiry/atomicity, duplicate/invalid requests, strict unknown-field rejection, exact password spaces, normalized login/recovery and optional authenticated actor. `AuthInputContractTest` proves all six DTOs are strict, non-auth JSON stays tolerant, and secrets remain exact; `PostgresCriticalPathIntegrationTest.emailIndexRejectsConcurrentCaseVariedLogicalDuplicates` proves the existing lower(email) unique index under concurrency; `EmailServiceTest.disabledDeliveryNeverCallsProvider` proves disabled adapter does not touch Resend. Existing `AuthServiceTest.registerAndLoginIssueTokensWithoutPersistingRawRefreshToken` covers service token issuance; `AccountEmailNotificationServiceTest` covers content. MANUAL FRONTEND: rendered identity/navigation/reload/sign-out and explicit `/auth/me` comparison; one-off browser evidence does not constitute a committed browser suite. STAGING EMAIL ONLY: actual delivery/CTA. No browser framework added.

**Environment requirement:** LOCAL REAL POSTGRES for A and API/integration assertions; browser frontend at localhost:3000, backend localhost:8080/api. Testcontainers uses the existing `-Ppostgres-integration` profile and common migrations; local Compose additionally uses dev seeds. STAGING for B only. Neither provider-disabled local success nor simulated delivery failure proves actual deliverability.

**Source/evidence:** Backend `controller/AuthController`, `dto/request/{RegisterRequest,LoginRequest,EmailAddressRequest,StrictAuthRequest,EmailNormalizer}`, `dto/response/{AuthResponse,UserDto}`, `service/{AuthService,AccountRecoveryService,OneTimeTokenCodec,AccountEmailEventListener,AccountEmailNotificationService,EmailService}`, `security/{JwtService,JwtAuthenticationFilter}`, `security/SecurityConfig`, `entity/{User,RefreshToken,EmailVerificationToken}`, repositories, common migrations V1/V8, dev V100–V102, `exception/GlobalExceptionHandler`; frontend `components/auth/{AuthPanel,AuthProvider}`, `components/layout/AppHeader`, `app/page.tsx`, `lib/api/{auth,client}.ts`, `lib/auth/token.ts`. Reproduction/evidence: [companion guide](qa/AUTH-001_REGISTER_SCOUT.md).

**Pass/fail criteria:** A passes only if local HTTP/DB/security/transaction checks and browser registration/reload/cleanup all meet the above, with dated sanitized evidence. B has its own delivery result. FAIL for a mismatch or unexpected side effect; BLOCKED for missing infrastructure/evidence; NOT RUN for unexecuted checks. Never infer B PASS from A or mark unrelated AUTH scenarios passed.

**Test ID:** AUTH-003. **Area:** AUTH. **Priority:** P0. **Test level:** API, INTEGRATION, LOCAL E2E, SECURITY. **Result:** LOCAL PASS (2026-09-10); real delivery STAGING ONLY / NOT RUN where applicable.

<a id="family-trust"></a>
### TRUST scenarios

<a id="trust-001"></a>
#### TRUST-001 — Owner review lifecycle, audit and first-submission concurrency

**Area:** TRUST · **Priority:** P0 · **Test level:** HTTP, PostgreSQL, browser · **Result:** PASS (local software; staging/operations follow-ups separate)

**Actual actors/prerequisites:** Active OWNER; current DB email verification required for submission, not GET. ADMIN reviews; no admin email-verification prerequisite. Neither actor needs policy acceptance. Use unique RUN_ID fictional accounts; email delivery disabled locally.

**Exact API journey:** GET /api/owner/verification synthesizes UNVERIFIED with null ID before first submission without creating a row. POST /api/owner/verification/submit with optional QA note returns 200 PENDING. Duplicate PENDING submission returns 200 unchanged. ADMIN POST /api/admin/owner-verifications/{id}/reject with reason returns 200 REJECTED. Owner resubmits (200 PENDING, same ID); admin approves with MANUAL_REVIEW (200 VERIFIED).

**Persistence/audit:** One row per owner. Initial submission records ownerNote/submittedAt and version 0. Duplicate changes neither note nor timestamps/version and emits no event. Rejection records reviewer/reviewedAt/trimmed owner-visible reason, no method. Resubmission replaces ownerNote/submittedAt and clears all review fields. Approval records reviewer/time/method/optional note. Audit sequence SUBMITTED, REJECTED, SUBMITTED, APPROVED retains correct subject and OWNER/ADMIN actor; only rejection carries the reason. Current entity fields do not preserve previous owner/approval notes as separate audit evidence.

**Browser:** Owner UNVERIFIED → PENDING → reload → owner-visible rejection → resubmit → VERIFIED → reload. Admin queue/detail, explicit reject/approve confirmation. Owner consumes Spring's returned DTO; admin reloads from Spring. No locally invented status.

**Notifications:** Every legitimate submission/resubmission, rejection and approval emits an asynchronous AFTER_COMMIT lifecycle notification. Disabled EmailService skips delivery; listener failure cannot roll back the committed transition. Duplicate pending and denied/invalid commands emit none. Real Resend delivery remains staging-only.

**Concurrency:** Barrier-coordinated simultaneous first submissions use real PostgreSQL: both 200, same ID, one PENDING row and one submission audit/notification. Lock the existing owner before looking up the potentially absent verification. Reject/resubmit race must serialize to a valid lifecycle without mixed review fields.

**Automation:** OwnerTrustIntegrationTest lifecycle, simultaneousFirstSubmissionIsOneCommittedLifecycle, rejectionVersusResubmissionHasOnlyLegalOrderedOutcomes, notificationRunsAfterCommitAndFailureCannotRollBackTrust; TrustNotificationServiceTest and EmailServiceTest; scripts/qa/trust-browser.cjs.

**Cleanup/limits:** Dispose Testcontainers DB and dedicated browser QA DB/profile; discard session credentials. Never delete shared trust history or restore a fictional snapshot. Operations must define manual review criteria/SLA; software execution does not approve them. See docs/qa/TRUST_EXECUTION_REPORT.md and docs/qa/evidence/trust/.

<a id="trust-002"></a>
#### TRUST-002 — Actor, transition and trust-boundary enforcement

**Area:** TRUST · **Priority:** P0 · **Test level:** HTTP, PostgreSQL, browser · **Result:** PASS (local software; staging/operations follow-ups separate)

**Actual actors/prerequisites:** OWNER owns the implicit current-user endpoint; no owner UUID parameter exists. ADMIN alone lists/gets/reviews admin records. Fixtures include verified/unverified OWNER, SCOUT, ADMIN and anonymous; no policy prerequisite.

**Authorization:** Owner GET: OWNER 200 including unverified email; SCOUT/ADMIN 403; anonymous 401. Owner submit: verified active OWNER 200, unverified OWNER/SCOUT/ADMIN 403, anonymous/inactive 401. Admin list/detail/approve/reject: ADMIN allowed, OWNER/SCOUT 403, anonymous 401. Verify controller and global /admin security. Current DB email/active/role state controls authorization even with an older token.

**Transitions:** VERIFIED submit is 409 and preserves review method/time. Only PENDING can be approved/rejected; VERIFIED, REJECTED and persisted schema-valid UNVERIFIED return 409. Logical no-row UNVERIFIED has no review ID; a nonexistent UUID returns 404. Repeat review is 409. Denied/invalid calls leave row/version/audit/notifications unchanged.

**Separation/privacy:** Approval must leave existing DRAFT/PENDING venues unchanged and create no payout destination/payout or identity/bank evidence. Owner DTO contains id, ownerId, status, submittedAt, reviewedAt, reviewNote, verificationMethod; no reviewer ID or private operations fields. Admin DTO adds ownerNote, reviewedBy, createdAt/updatedAt. Queue filters status/ownerId and caps page size at 100.

**Concurrency/browser:** Real PostgreSQL approve/approve and approve/reject races yield one 200 and one 409; exactly one consistent review/audit wins. Browser wrong-role guards, missing review, safe validation/session/network errors; stale admin decision refetches authoritative state and keeps actionable conflict text visible after PENDING controls disappear.

**Automation:** OwnerTrustIntegrationTest currentDbEmailRoleAndAdminSecurityAreAuthoritative, onlyPendingCanBeReviewedAndApprovalHasNoVenueOrBankSideEffects, queueFiltersProjectionAndDatabaseConstraints, competingAdminReviewsHaveOneWinner; existing security annotations/AUTH current-user tests; scripts/qa/trust-browser.cjs.

**Cleanup/limits:** Unique accounts in disposable PostgreSQL, isolated browser session; no deletion of shared audit history. No revoke/downgrade operation exists. Any future revocation or reviewer-note visibility change requires an operations/product decision.

<a id="trust-003"></a>

**Area:** TRUST · **Priority:** P0 · **Test level:** parameterized HTTP/PostgreSQL, browser · **Result:** PASS (local software; staging/operations follow-ups separate)

**Actual actors/prerequisites:** Verified-email OWNER submits; ADMIN approves an independent PENDING owner per method. No policy acceptance prerequisite.

Missing/null/unknown method returns 400 with no transition. **Unknown fields:** Record DTO binding safely ignores unknown properties; injected ownerId/status/reviewedAt cannot assign entity state. Do not impose unrelated AUTH strict-JSON rules.

No sensitive evidence upload is supported; do not collect or attach real evidence for QA.

<a id="family-ready"></a>
### READY scenarios

<a id="ready-001"></a>
#### READY-001 — Readiness issue maxCrewSize

**Area:** READY · **Priority:** P1 · **Test level:** UNIT + service + PostgreSQL; representative browser · **Result:** PASS — local deterministic contract; UX/operations/staging limits remain

**Actors/prerequisites:** Validator has no actor. Workflow fixture: active verified-email owning OWNER, owner review VERIFIED, current policies accepted; ADMIN reviews/reactivates. No repeated unrelated ownership checks; VEN covers authorization.

**Exact contract:** Clear maxCrewSize to null: exact issue maxCrewSize. Restore 20: no issues. Zero/negative and DTO maximum 10,000 belong to numeric validation, not readiness presence.

**Execution and effects:** Start from the centralized complete fixture with no issues. Remove only this condition; assert exact single issue, no mutation; restore and assert empty. Submit/approve/reactivate must refuse readiness-incomplete fixtures before changing status, timestamps, trust events or notifications. Restore then transition successfully. Use real API/PG only for reachable absent states; never insert an impossible row or disable a constraint.

### MEDIA scenarios

<a id="media-001"></a>
#### MEDIA-001 — Valid image upload and durable reference

**Area:** MEDIA · **Priority:** P1 · **Test level:** UNIT, API, REAL POSTGRES, LOCAL FILESYSTEM, BROWSER · **Result:** PASS (LOCAL; staging/privacy decisions separate)

**Actors/prerequisites:** Standalone upload: authenticated, verified-email OWNER; ADMIN and SCOUT denied 403, anonymous 401. Scoped upload: own verified-email OWNER or ADMIN (email exemption); other OWNER/SCOUT 403, anonymous 401. Neither policies nor owner verification is required. Unique RUN_ID venues; no shared fixture reset.

**Actual endpoints:** POST `/api/upload/venue-photo`, multipart `file`, returns 200 `{message,url}` and stores only. POST `/api/venues/{id}/photos`, multipart `file`, returns 200 authoritative VenueDto after locked append and persistence. GET `/api/upload/files/{filename}` is public and proxies local/S3 bytes.

**Steps/assertions:** Upload real decodable JPEG (.jpg/.jpeg), PNG and WebP. Confirm generated UUID key, controlled reference, exact bytes/Content-Type/nosniff on public read, original filename discarded, scoped ordered DB attachment, and standalone no attachment. Reload editor and restart the production-Dockerfile backend with a dedicated named media volume; references and bytes survive. S3 mock verifies bucket/prefix/content type, conditional create and proxy read; it does not prove deployed storage.

**Side effects:** Ordinary DRAFT upload has no moderation event/email. Owner ACTIVE photo change invokes re-review and VENUE_SUBMITTED notification; ADMIN retains existing override behavior. Local emails disabled; actual delivery belongs to staging.

**Automation/cleanup/limits:** `MediaStorageContractTest`, `VenueDomainIntegrationTest#media*`, `scripts/qa/media-browser.cjs`. Disposable Testcontainers, temporary media root, dedicated compose volume/browser profile. Dispose whole QA environment, never shared media/history. Human gallery UX and deployed S3 durability/access remain separate; see `docs/qa/MEDIA_EXECUTION_REPORT.md`.

<a id="media-002"></a>
#### MEDIA-002 — Image content, size, multipart and public-path security

**Area:** MEDIA · **Priority:** P1 · **Test level:** PARAMETERIZED UNIT, API, REAL POSTGRES, REAL HTTP · **Result:** PASS (LOCAL; staging/privacy decisions separate)

**Actors/prerequisites:** Use an authorized actor from MEDIA-001 and an owned DRAFT to isolate validation. Reuse endpoint authorization matrix; there is no standalone resource-ownership UUID.

**Steps/assertions:** Both adapters reject empty, one-byte, truncated/fake image, GIF/SVG/BMP/text/octet-stream, missing/unsupported filename/type, MIME-extension mismatch and decoded-format mismatch before durable write. Validate JPEG/PNG with ImageIO and WebP with TwelveMonkeys; headers/extensions alone are not proof. Decode only after geometry checks: ≤10,000 pixels per side and ≤25 million pixels total, at most two decoders/JVM. No re-encoding, EXIF stripping or malware scanning is claimed.

**Boundary layers:** Default file limit 5,242,880 bytes. A decodable JPEG padded to exactly 5 MiB succeeds; +1 fails storage validation with 400 in service/MockMvc, and the real servlet rejects oversized multipart with 413. Missing part, malformed multipart and non-multipart upload requests return 400. Parameterize unsafe client filenames: generated UUID ignores all path components. Public nonexistent/invalid/traversal/private-document names cannot expose files; valid-shaped symlinks are refused. Missing object 404.

**Persistence/side effects:** Invalid and denied uploads leave no new object, photo reference, moderation event or lifecycle email. No raw provider error, bytes or credentials in client response. Browser errors explain corrupt/type/size failures; HTML accept attribute is UX only.

**Automation/cleanup/limits:** Shared binary fixtures and parameterized `MediaStorageContractTest`, `VenueDomainIntegrationTest#mediaAuthorizationInvalidContentAndMaxLimitNeverLeaveOrphans`, representative real-browser/HTTP runner. Temporary media/disposable DB; preserve shared objects. Pre-change fake bytes acceptance was a reproduced P1 defect, not acceptable behavior. Existing legacy objects are not retroactively validated. Privacy/EXIF and staging object permissions require separate decisions.

<a id="media-003"></a>
#### MEDIA-003 — Ordered photos, maximum, readiness and moderation

**Area:** MEDIA · **Priority:** P1 · **Test level:** API, REAL POSTGRES, BROWSER · **Result:** PASS (LOCAL; staging/privacy decisions separate)

**Actors/prerequisites:** Own verified-email OWNER or ADMIN for scoped upload/PUT; use independent ACTIVE fixture only for moderation case. ADMIN edit override is an existing operations decision, not changed here.

**Steps/assertions:** Upload A/B/C and persist `[A,B,C]`; first reference is primary in editor/card/detail. Full PUT `[C,A,B]` changes order without copying bytes. PUT `[B,C]` detaches A, with no physical deletion promise. Empty list restores photo readiness issue; first attachment removes it. Accept 1/11/12 photos and reject the thirteenth before storage. Reject duplicate references, external/file/traversal/non-UUID references and >12 arrays without mutation. Reference shape does not establish existence or exclusive ownership; do not invent that guarantee.

**Moderation/concurrency:** Owner ACTIVE add/remove/reorder → PENDING with existing re-review event/notification; historical booking behavior is covered by VEN. Ordinary DRAFT reorder/remove has no email. Real PostgreSQL barriers prove two successful simultaneous uploads both persist exactly once; at 11 one wins and one safely fails, with no orphan. Concurrent full PUT/upload serializes, but a later stale whole-array PUT may detach the uploaded reference; row locking does not provide client revision detection.

**Automation/cleanup/limits:** Reuse VEN photo criticality/READY-012 and add `VenueDomainIntegrationTest#mediaConcurrent*`, max-limit/reorder checks and representative browser primary/removal/12-photo journey. Repeat race groups; no timing sleeps. Dispose unique test environment. Orphans (standalone, detached, abandoned draft) remain an operations backlog; no GC or ownership table is introduced.

<a id="media-004"></a>
#### MEDIA-004 — Storage compensation after persistence failure

**Area:** MEDIA · **Priority:** P1 · **Test level:** SERVICE, REAL POSTGRES, S3 MOCK · **Result:** PASS (LOCAL; staging/privacy decisions separate)

**Actors/prerequisites:** Own verified-email OWNER with room for a photo, valid real image; use test-controlled persistence failure after storage succeeds. No provider credentials or shared-row deletion.

**Steps/assertions:** Scoped upload writes object, then save/saveAndFlush fails. Original persistence exception remains primary; deletion of the newly unattached object is attempted. Real PostgreSQL flush-then-fail proves transaction rollback: unchanged photo array/status/trust events and no after-commit notification. Repeat with delete failure; retain original error, log only safe venue/reference/error-class metadata, never report success. Mock S3 verifies deletion bucket/key.

**Transaction limitation:** Object storage is outside the DB transaction. Immediate save/flush compensation does not guarantee cleanup if transaction completion fails after the service returns, or process death/delete failure occurs. These are explicitly recorded orphan risks; no garbage collection is claimed.

**Automation/cleanup/limits:** `VenueServiceTest` persistence/delete-failure checks; `VenueDomainIntegrationTest#mediaAttachmentFailureAfterRealFlushRollsBackRowsAndDeletesNewObject`; S3 adapter mock contract. Temporary filesystem and disposable Testcontainers only. Real provider outages, credentials, lifecycle retention and orphan monitoring remain staging/operations work, not manual deterministic DB testing.


<a id="family-avl"></a>
### AVL scenarios

**Shared AVL execution contract:** Spring computes normalized weekly ∪ AVAILABLE, subtracts BLOCKED ∪ reserving bookings, clips by elapsed lead time in venue timezone, then normalizes. Intervals are ordered same-day half-open [start,end); adjacent union intervals merge. Empty week is empty base, not 24/7. ACTIVE means approved listing, not guaranteed current slots.

**Actors and isolation:** Public effective GET respects venue visibility (ACTIVE public; non-ACTIVE own OWNER/ADMIN). Settings GET is own OWNER/ADMIN; anonymous returns403 under the public GET route plus method guard. Mutation is own verified-email OWNER or ADMIN (email exemption); other OWNER/SCOUT403, anonymous401. No owner review/current policies needed for ordinary settings changes. Use unique RUN_ID fixtures, fixed test Clock, disposable Testcontainers and isolated browser DB/profile; never delete shared history or restore fictional snapshots. Schedule mutations have no lifecycle email. Booking/inquiry expiry retains real lifecycle events; email delivery is separate.

No fictional snapshot restore or deletion of shared history. See docs/qa/MATCH_EXECUTION_REPORT.md and docs/qa/evidence/match/. Local PASS proves mapping/containment, never live Gemini extraction accuracy or explanation truthfulness. Live language/model/privacy/operations approval remains separate.

### BK scenarios

The BK contract is audited against BookingService, BookingStateMachine, BookingController, BookingAvailabilityValidator, BookingReservationPolicy and V1 exclusion constraint. Execution/evidence: [BK execution report](qa/BK_EXECUTION_REPORT.md). Payment settlement, refunds and payouts remain separate domains.

**Shared environment / cleanup:** UNIT and real disposable PostgreSQL via `mvn verify -Ppostgres-integration`; unique fictional RUN_ID accounts/venues; fixed Clock for core deadlines; isolated Chrome profile. Never delete shared booking, policy or audit history. QA policies say “QA TEST CONTENT — NOT LEGAL TERMS”. No fake snapshot reset.

**Shared prerequisites:** SCOUT request and OWNER response need active account, verified email and all current required policies. ADMIN response is explicitly supported and exempt from email/policy acceptance, but ADMIN cannot create a scout request. Booking endpoints do not directly require owner verification. Request venue must be ACTIVE and interval satisfy availability/lead time. Read history remains available after policy replacement. Unit fixtures have no irrelevant role prerequisites.

**Notification boundary:** Request publication targets owner + scout; acceptance, decline, request expiry and unavailable target scout. After-commit listener contains delivery failures and suppresses stale status notifications. Denied/invalid operations do not publish lifecycle transitions, except deadline/lead-time acceptance conflicts deliberately commit request expiry. Request and acceptance create no provider payment/refund. Local email-disabled mode is not real delivery proof. Human UX and staging email/deployment review remain separate from local software results.

<a id="family-inq"></a>
### INQ scenarios

**Execution:** [INQ execution report](qa/INQ_EXECUTION_REPORT.md). Source is authoritative; the four IDs map to parameterized HTTP/PostgreSQL matrices and a representative real browser journey.

**Shared fixtures/cleanup:** Unique fictional QA users and venues, fixed Clock, disposable PostgreSQL Testcontainers, isolated Chrome profile; temporary auth configuration is mode 0600 and removed after execution. Do not delete shared inquiry/booking history or restore a nonexistent snapshot. No real payment or email provider calls. Unit notification tests and local disabled-email logs prove software behavior; deployed delivery is separate.

**State model:** OPEN → OFFERED/DECLINED; OFFERED → ACCEPTED/EXPIRED. OPEN and OFFERED are not reservations. Acceptance alone creates AWAITING_PAYMENT and a unique booking link atomically. Inquiry actions never write weekly operating hours or availability overrides. No custom offer price, offer revision/withdrawal, scout decline, OPEN expiry, or inquiry event-history table exists.

<a id="inq-001"></a>
#### INQ-001 — Unavailable-slot inquiry creation

**Area:** INQ · **Priority:** P1 · **Test level:** API, REAL POSTGRES, BROWSER REPRESENTATIVE · **Result:** PASS locally — see execution report

**Actors/prerequisites:** Active, verified-email SCOUT with current policies; ACTIVE venue and valid interval meeting venue lead time. No scout owner-verification/payout requirement. OWNER/ADMIN 403, anonymous 401. GET mine is SCOUT-only; GET owned-venues OWNER-only. Lists are actor-scoped and do not require policy acceptance.

**Contract:** POST `/availability-inquiries` with venueId, requestedDate, requestedStartTime, requestedEndTime, message. Outside weekly 09–17, D14 18–20 returns 201 OPEN. Exact local requested times/message persist; DTO timezone is current venue metadata, not a historical timezone snapshot. Normally available 09–11 returns 400 directing normal booking requests, including with an overlapping non-blocking REQUESTED booking. A blocking booking may make an inquiry eligible, but cannot be bypassed during offer/accept.

**Validation:** Nonblank message max 1000 before service trim; null/empty/whitespace/1001→400, one character/1000→201. Browser empty input supplies “I'd like to ask about this time.” Invalid/missing date/time or same-day unordered interval→400; past/too-soon valid interval→409 via lead policy. Exact lead threshold allowed. Non-ACTIVE→404. Unknown command fields cannot set status/link.

**Persistence/side effects:** One OPEN row and CREATED lifecycle event/email to owner; no booking, reservation, calendar mutation or payment. Denied/invalid requests leave no row/event/notification. Dashboard DTO has no contact/private financial data; owner creation email currently includes scout contact information, documented for privacy review. React renders message as text.

**Automation:** InquiryIntegrationTest message, invalid creation, routing, exact lead, actor/read/privacy matrices; existing AvailabilityInquiryServiceTest and AvailabilityInquiryNotificationServiceTest; InquiryBrowserIntegrationTest calendar mode/fallback/OPEN. Shared cleanup above. Human review is wording and flow clarity, not binary/API edge cases.

<a id="inq-002"></a>
#### INQ-002 — Owner offers same or different one-off slot

**Area:** INQ · **Priority:** P1 · **Test level:** API, REAL POSTGRES, BROWSER REPRESENTATIVE · **Result:** PASS locally — see execution report

**Actors/prerequisites:** Only the venue's active verified-email OWNER with current policies may POST `/{id}/offer`; other owner/scouts/ADMIN 403, anonymous 401. Existing OPEN inquiry, ACTIVE venue, ordered valid offered interval meeting lead time and no blocking overlap.

**Contract:** Body offeredDate/offeredStartTime/offeredEndTime; same or different slot allowed, including outside weekly hours or through calendar BLOCKED overrides. Existing AWAITING_PAYMENT/CONFIRMED overlap→409; other booking statuses do not block. Half-open adjacency is legal. Expiry is min(now+configured 48h default, offered slot start in venue timezone). Duplicate/non-OPEN offer→409 with no rewrite or expiry extension. Missing/malformed fields→400; past/too-soon→409. Suspended venue→409, no OFFERED transition.

**Persistence/side effects:** Preserve requested interval; persist offered interval/offeredAt/offerExpiresAt and OFFERED status. One OFFERED lifecycle notification to scout. No booking, price snapshot, reservation or calendar write. Offers serialize with venue moderation; an offer remains non-blocking even after successful save.

**Automation:** InquiryIntegrationTest blocking-status/adjacency, expiry cap, exact lead, invalid offer, all-state/action, current account/policy and suspension cases. Browser requested versus different offered time, reload, stale owner offer/decline conflict refetch with retained feedback. Shared cleanup above. Product decisions: price locking, temporary reservation and offer revision are not implemented by this test pass.

<a id="inq-003"></a>
#### INQ-003 — Atomic offer acceptance and late conflict

**Area:** INQ · **Priority:** P0 · **Test level:** API, REAL POSTGRES, BROWSER REPRESENTATIVE · **Result:** PASS locally — see execution report

**Actors/prerequisites:** Only originating active verified-email SCOUT with current policies accepts via POST `/{id}/accept`; other scout/owners/ADMIN 403, anonymous 401. OFFERED, before expiry, ACTIVE venue, valid lead time and no blocking overlap. No ordinary weekly-availability requirement for the exception booking.

**Contract:** Returns 200 BookingDto directly AWAITING_PAYMENT; inquiry ACCEPTED with acceptedBookingId. Standard payment deadline defaults acceptance+24h; no owner-response deadline or second owner acceptance. Current authoritative venue price/commission/live participant contacts/four booking policy references are snapshotted at conversion. Offer is not a price lock. Normal shared checkout uses stored booking amount (mocked provider only).

**Late outcomes:** At/after offerExpiresAt→409, remains OFFERED until worker expires it. Lead failure→EXPIRED committed before 409. Occupied→409 remains OFFERED. Non-ACTIVE→404 remains OFFERED. Duplicate acceptance→409 with original single booking/link. Missing ID 404/malformed UUID 400. No failed path may leave ACCEPTED with a missing booking.

**Persistence/concurrency:** Same-inquiry lock plus venue lock serializes double acceptance, different overlapping offers, normal reservation and suspension. PostgreSQL exclusion permits exactly one blocking reservation. Added stricter disposable-DB failure injection proves booking/policy/audit writes roll back if inquiry save fails and no after-commit success notification is emitted. Calendar tables remain unchanged; the created booking now blocks inventory.

**Events/UI:** Only booking REQUEST_ACCEPTED event with source availability_inquiry and its scout payment notification; no duplicate inquiry-accepted event/email. Browser accepts, redirects `/bookings/{id}`, reloads AWAITING_PAYMENT; stale acceptance refetches and retains safe feedback. No real Mollie call or payment success claim.

**Automation:** InquiryIntegrationTest conversion snapshots/shared mocked checkout, deadlines, policy replacement, changed account authority, atomicity, repeated double/two-offer/normal-accept/suspension races; BK/AVL exclusion and checkout tests reused. InquiryBrowserIntegrationTest. Shared cleanup above. Product review: current acceptance-time price and live venue timezone semantics.

<a id="inq-004"></a>
#### INQ-004 — Decline, expiry and scoped dashboard history

**Area:** INQ · **Priority:** P1 · **Test level:** API, REAL POSTGRES, BROWSER REPRESENTATIVE · **Result:** PASS locally — see execution report

**Actors/prerequisites:** Own verified-email/current-policy OWNER declines OPEN via POST `/{id}/decline`; no ADMIN delegation. Decline does not require ACTIVE because it creates no commitment. Other actors 403/anonymous 401. No decline reason field exists. Only due OFFERED rows expire.

**Contract:** OPEN→DECLINED with declinedAt; duplicate/other status→409 without extra notification. Worker `expireOffers(now)` locks at most 100 due offers with SKIP LOCKED; OFFERED→EXPIRED with expiredAt and one OFFER_EXPIRED notification. Repeated processing is idempotent. Default scan 60s; direct accept rejects overdue offers independently of scheduler. OPEN has no response deadline/expiry.

**Persistence/notifications:** Neither decline nor expiry creates booking/payment/refund/calendar changes. DECLINED email means inquiry declined, not booking declined. OFFER_EXPIRED means offer expired. Application lifecycle events are not a persisted inquiry timeline; booking audit begins at conversion.

**Dashboard/privacy:** `/scout/inquiries` shows own waiting/declined/offered/expired/accepted history and booking link; `/owner/inquiries` only owned-venue inquiries. Original requested and offered intervals both remain visible; expiry uses venue timezone even with a different browser timezone. No contact data is added to inquiry DTO/UI. Lists currently unpaginated.

**Automation:** InquiryIntegrationTest five-state×four-action matrix, actor-scoped reads, repeated expiry/idempotency; PostgresCriticalPathIntegrationTest inquiry SKIP LOCKED disjoint-worker coverage; existing notification recipient/template/failure tests; representative browser decline/stale refetch/offer/accept. Shared cleanup above. Human UX and real deployed email/scheduler behavior remain separately listed in execution report.

<a id="family-price"></a>
### PRICE scenarios — audited 2026-09-15

**Source authority:** `BookingPriceCalculator`, venue DTO/entity money constraints, `BookingService`, `PaymentCreationCoordinator`, `BookingFinancials`, cancellation/payout accounting, receipt renderer and frontend `lib/pricing.ts`. Execution and defects: [PRICE execution report](qa/PRICE_EXECUTION_REPORT.md); evidence: `docs/qa/evidence/price/`.

**Shared contract:** selected duration is same-date LocalTime minutes. Billable minutes = max(selected, minimum). Hourly total = rate × billable /60 rounded to two decimals HALF_UP. Optional cap is separately normalized to two decimals HALF_UP; final price = min(rounded hourly total, normalized cap). Cap changes money, never selected/billable minutes. Minimum is a billing minimum, not a minimum selectable interval. No hidden quarter/hour increments. Overnight intervals are unsupported. DST billing uses selected wall-clock minutes; elapsed-time scheduling remains a separate contract.

**Execution:** all eleven IDs map to one parameterized `PriceContractTest` shared fixture and `scripts/qa/price-client-check.cjs`; exact cent parity, no tolerance. No actors, authentication, policies, database, clock, emails or providers are required for pure math. Representative PRICE-001/006/007/010 use actual HTTP/real PostgreSQL in `PriceIntegrationTest` to verify immutable snapshots and mocked checkout. Browser representatives cover minimum, prorating, cap, uncapped price and server price winning over a stale preview. No live Mollie payment is claimed.

**Money authority:** preview is indicative. Spring snapshots price/rate/minimum/cap/durations/commission at normal request creation or inquiry acceptance. Acceptance never reprices an existing booking. Checkout ignores client monetary fields and uses `Booking.venuePriceEur`. Commission, cancellation, payout and receipt consume stored historical economics. Matching before duration only describes rate/minimum/optional cap.

**Bounds:** rate/cap DTOs require 0.01..99,999,999.99; minimum 1..10,080. Fractional-cent configuration remains accepted and now normalizes to PostgreSQL cents before returning a venue DTO. Sub-minute selected duration and a final price exceeding NUMERIC(10,2) fail safely with HTTP 400 before booking persistence. A fitting cap may bring a large uncapped calculation into range. Positive settings can still round to 0.00: documented accounting decision, not an invented minimum price or verified provider capability.

**Cleanup:** shared deterministic fixtures, unique fictional QA accounts/venues, disposable Testcontainers PostgreSQL, isolated Chrome profile and temporary auth config. Never delete shared booking history. Successful booking integration has existing BK lifecycle notifications; pure pricing has none; provider transport is mocked locally.

Run shared fixture `PRICE-011` through Java calculator and actual frontend pricing module. Assert selected=301, billable=301, rounded hourly=501.67, final=500.00 exactly. Assert frontend returns the same cent amount. Shared snapshot, downstream and browser evidence applies as described above; no duplicated authorization matrix or database arithmetic implementation.

**Local conclusion:** canonical PRICE-001–011 pass unchanged. PRICE-DEF-005, previously an unresolved accounting decision, is resolved by the explicit Eema v1 policy: free bookings are not supported. After the unchanged exact-minute/minimum/hourly/HALF_UP/normalized-cap calculation, a final total below EUR 0.01 is rejected with HTTP 400 before booking persistence/payment creation. Inquiry acceptance remains coherently OFFERED on rejection. PRICE-008 remains valid at EUR 0.01. Checkout refuses legacy/corrupt stored amounts below EUR 0.01 without recomputation or provider interaction. Common migration V13 enforces the original-price invariant without changing legitimate zero paid/refund/payout amounts. Eight PostgreSQL and three service regression cases plus full backend verification passed; historical evidence and staging boundaries remain in the PRICE report.

<a id="family-pay"></a>
### PAY — Payment execution contract (audited 2026-09-15)

**Authority:** `PaymentCreationCoordinator`, `PaymentService`, `HttpMollieProviderClient`, `WebhookService`, locked `BookingService.processPaidPayment`, `RefundCoordinator`, and server-read frontend `/booked`. Full evidence, defects and limits: [PAY execution report](qa/PAY_EXECUTION_REPORT.md), `docs/qa/evidence/payment/`.

**Three separate state machines:** Booking `REQUESTED → AWAITING_PAYMENT → CONFIRMED`, or `AWAITING_PAYMENT → EXPIRED`. Payment creation `NOT_STARTED → CREATING → CREATED`. Refund `NONE → CREATING → QUEUED/PENDING/PROCESSING → REFUNDED`, with FAILED/CANCELED outcomes. A late paid booking stays EXPIRED while its refund progresses. No PENDING/PAID booking states, redirect confirmation, or second owner confirmation.

**Shared execution:** one parameterized `PaymentIntegrationTest` uses real PostgreSQL, fixed Clock and mocked Mollie; `PaymentTransportContractTest` verifies actual adapter payload/JSON handling and log redaction. Existing PRICE/BK/INQ/notification/payout coverage is referenced, not copied. `PaymentBrowserIntegrationTest` runs a representative real Chrome/UI/API journey with controlled provider navigation. Mocks do not establish real Mollie behavior.

**Actors:** checkout uses current active/verified user policy, centralized current policy acceptance and exact booking.scoutId ownership. No delegated owner/ADMIN checkout; normal unrelated actors403, anonymous401. An ADMIN policy exemption does not grant another scout's payment authority. Webhook is public form POST and fetches provider facts server-side.

**Cleanup:** unique fictional users/venues/bookings in disposable Testcontainers PostgreSQL; isolated browser profile and temporary auth config removed afterward. No shared staging history deletion, no fictitious fixture snapshot restoration. Real delivery, provider replay and deployed permissions remain staging checks.

<a id="pay-003"></a>
#### PAY-003 — Durable creation identity and concurrency

**Result:** LOCAL PASS — see [PAY execution report](qa/PAY_EXECUTION_REPORT.md); current full PostgreSQL regression also passes.

**Layer:** REAL POSTGRES / REPEATED BARRIER RACE. **Priority:** P0 payment integrity.

Claim/key/start time commit before external creation. Concurrent CREATING callers may perform multiple same-key HTTP requests, but never create independent identities. Three barrier repetitions inspect the committed row from provider callback and assert identical keys/results. CREATED retry returns stored ID/URL without new create. Fresh coordinator instance reuses persisted CREATING/CREATED state. In-flight valid response arriving after expiry stores its association, leaves EXPIRED and returns409 so a later callback can be refunded. This is service-boundary durability proof, not a live process-crash/provider experiment.

**Evidence:** `PaymentIntegrationTest`, transport/unit references and representative browser evidence mapped in [PAY report](qa/PAY_EXECUTION_REPORT.md).

<a id="pay-004"></a>
#### PAY-004 — Ambiguous creation and replay window

**Result:** LOCAL PASS — see [PAY execution report](qa/PAY_EXECUTION_REPORT.md); current full PostgreSQL regression also passes.

**Layer:** FIXED-CLOCK API / REAL POSTGRES. **Priority:** P0 payment integrity.

Transport timeout preserves CREATING, key and original start. At59 minutes and exactly60 minutes current local code permits same-key retry;61 minutes returns409 with no create call. One hour is a source constant, not configurable. No new identity after uncertainty. Existing PAYMENT_CREATION_STUCK exception queue/metric supports manual reconciliation. Mollie documentation says within one hour; exact provider-edge replay remains staging verification, not inferred from the local equality test.

**Evidence:** `PaymentIntegrationTest`, transport/unit references and representative browser evidence mapped in [PAY report](qa/PAY_EXECUTION_REPORT.md).

<a id="ref-002"></a>

#### REF-002 — Validated monotonic refund lifecycle and origin-sensitive completion

**Area:** REF · **Priority:** P0 · **Test level:** real PostgreSQL API/service integration + separate transport/unit contracts · **Result:** PASS (local)

**Exact states:** NONE, CREATING, QUEUED, PENDING, PROCESSING, REFUNDED, FAILED, CANCELED. NONE/CREATING are local states; provider `creating` is invalid. CREATING accepts any real provider state; QUEUED → PENDING/PROCESSING/REFUNDED/FAILED/CANCELED; PENDING → PROCESSING/REFUNDED/FAILED/CANCELED; PROCESSING → REFUNDED/FAILED. All three terminal states are absorbing; equality/stale regressions have no effects.

**Provider checks:** Validate payment ID, attached refund ID, persisted claim association, exact EUR amount and supported status before a transition. Parameterize missing/wrong fields, EUR currency, amount format and unknown status. Invalid facts must not complete or alter economics. The abstraction does not expose echoed claim metadata or list/search; before ID attachment it cannot independently distinguish an unrelated same-payment/same-amount response.

**Completion:** Admin CONFIRMED → REFUNDED; cancellation stays CANCELLED; late safety refund stays EXPIRED. Set refundedAt once only on accepted completion. Repeated terminal responses produce one audit completion and one payout recalculation; cancellation emits one completion notification, admin emits none. FAILED/CANCELED never claim successful money movement or permit automatic rekeying.

**Evidence:** [REF execution report](qa/REF_EXECUTION_REPORT.md), [sanitized execution evidence](qa/evidence/refund/). `RefundIntegrationTest`, `RefundClaimContractTest`, shared `RefundCancellationContractTest` and separate `RefundTransportContractTest`. Local mocks prove Eema safety logic only. Real Mollie refunds, idempotency, statuses, settlement and actual emails remain staging-only.

The same payment, amount and key must survive. Test fixed Clock at 3,599 / 3,600 / 3,601 seconds: only strictly inside one hour permits remote retry; at/after the boundary expect 409 and manual reconciliation with no new provider creation.

**Errors:** Transport failure and HTTP 408/409/429/5xx preserve CREATING. Representative definitive HTTP 422 enters FAILED, retains the identity and returns sanitized support-review text. No raw provider body. No force-success or arbitrary provider-ID mutation exists.

**Concurrency/durability:** Repeat ambiguous restart and two simultaneous requests three times. Real PostgreSQL and provider barriers must show one claim, one logical mock-provider refund and no concurrency 500. Multiple transports may reuse the same provider idempotency key. Reuse existing shared pre-call rollback/post-call persistence failure tests. V12 enforces amount <= paid amount and immutable claimed key/amount/payment and attached refund ID. **Fixture and steps:** Pay EUR 125.50, reconcile actual provider fee EUR 1.50, end the interval, prepare verified destination and calculate READY. ADMIN marks EUR 98.90 paid; snapshot the entire payout row. Initiate full refund and accept provider completion. Repeat lookup and payout recalculation twice.

**Expected accounting:** PAID row remains byte-for-byte unchanged, including amount, paidAt, reference and destination snapshot. Exactly one positive EUR 98.90 OWNER_PAYOUT_RECOVERY liability; no new transfer and no negative payout. Refund completion is independent of later liability settlement.

**Required race:** With real PostgreSQL booking locks and barriers, repeat each serialization three times. Refund claim first holds the stale READY payout and mark-paid conflicts. Transfer first preserves PAID and completion creates recovery liability. Neither path rewrites transfer history.

**Fee follow-up:** A fee may reconcile after admin refund; owner entitlement remains zero and payout is CANCELLED if never paid. Unknown cost is not estimated. Keep the existing CANCEL/PAYOUT accounting policy; do not invent a waiver or debt rule.
